35. Entry into the care system will have followed problems or trauma within the family unit;
perhaps illness or death of the caring parent; domestic abuse, either of the child directly or
within the family, leading to an unstable or dangerous environment; or drug and/or alcohol
problems which create a chaotic lifestyle for dependent children. See adverse childhood
experience (ACE) in chapter 4.

36. Many enter care because they have been abused or neglected. These experiences can
leave children with complex emotional and mental health needs, which can increase their
risk of experiencing a range of poor outcomes, including vulnerability to abuse.
469

37. Such difficult early issues may resonate throughout life, with effects on educational
attainment, mental health and attitudes to authority figures.
